title: Reporting Under Strain
description: With the reporting module's flake simulation dialed up, a dispatcher's scheduled report job must never end up in a corrupted or ambiguous state — it should always resolve cleanly to either ready or failed, even if the request that created it barely survived a simulated outage.
successCondition: With FLAKE_LATENCY_MS_REPORTING and FLAKE_FAILURE_RATE_REPORTING set to nonzero values, repeatedly (at least 5 times) call POST /api/reporting/jobs with a valid query. Every call either succeeds with 202 and a job in "pending" status, or fails with 503 { error: { code: "INTERNAL_ERROR" } } before a job was ever created (confirm via GET /api/reporting/jobs/:id on a captured id returning 404 for any call that 503'd, meaning nothing partial was persisted). For every job that did reach "pending", poll it until it resolves — within a reasonable timeout, its status becomes either "ready" (with a downloadable CSV) or "failed" (with a non-null failureReason), never stuck indefinitely in "pending".
hints: The flake hook rejects at the request level before the handler runs, so a 503 here means no ReportJob row was ever created — you can't check a job id you never received, so this hint is about not needing to check IDs you never got back.

Set the env vars before starting the API server — this requires control over server configuration, not just request payloads. If your test harness can't restart the server, focus on the polling-to-resolution half of this challenge with a lower failure rate.
